title: Oak Harbor Manufacturing — edge inference pilot scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Customer: Oak Harbor Manufacturing (assembly line QA + operator assist).
- Pilot goal: run a mid-size LLM for short-turn inference at the factory edge (air-gapped rack), provide realtime checklist suggestions and anomaly explanations for operators (~1–3 sentence responses).
- Primary constraint: no external network egress; KMS/HSM on customer subnet; hardware limited to 2x GPUs per node (they're evaluating A10 vs A5000 class).
- Desired latency SLO: p95 < 120ms for <= 64 tokens; p99 < 200ms for burst loads. Throughput: ~60–120 reqs/min sustained, with bursts up to 300 reqs/min during shift change.

Notes from 2026-02-18 call (initial technical intake):
- Oak Harbor wants simple REST API endpoint inside their VPC; will accept SDK shim or k8s service.
- Security: must use HSM-backed signing for model artifacts; audit logs retained for 90 days.
- Data residency: everything stays on-prem; they want offline model updates via signed tarball (S3-like staging server on network segment).
- Model preference: they want a smaller foundation model (7B-13B) quantized to reduce memory. They asked about int8 vs int4 tradeoffs for hallucination/regression.
- Ops team is small (2 infra, 1 ML). They prefer a packaged appliance (container + supervisor) over a full k8s install.
- Power/cooling: nodes are standard rack gear, thermal headroom limited — prefer lower-power GPUs or conservative sustained clocks.

Technical gotchas / risks callout:
- KV cache memory: With local operator workflows (lots of short convs), KV cache must be per-connection and memory budget per GPU is tight on 12–16GB cards. Need to calculate worst-case sequences.
- Quantization regressions: int4 at small model sizes sometimes increases repetition/hallucination for instruction-following tasks. Plan: A/B test int8 vs int4 on their prompt set.
- NUMA/CPU pinning: observed p95 spikes when CPU-GPU DMA is contended; the appliance must include NUMA-aware configuration and guidance for PCIe lanes.
- Cold-starts/warm pools: they will have burst patterns; warmup pods or pre-warmed persistent processes recommended (avoid ephemeral container startup for 1st requests).
- Air-gapped rollout: model updates via USB or local staging server — need artifact signing and deterministic upgrade steps.
- Licensing/compliance: confirm open-model license compatibility for on-prem use; they requested PDF of recommended models and licenses.

Initial checklist / measurement plan (things for pilot):
- Baseline perf: measure single-GPU memory footprint for 7B int8, 7B int4, and 13B int8 variants using their representative prompt distribution (median seq 48 tokens, max 256 tokens).
- Latency profile: p50/p95/p99 for 1, 4, 8 concurrent connections.
- Throughput scalability: synthetic load to validate sustained 120 reqs/min and burst 300 reqs/min with 2 GPUs.
- Quality evals: run their 120 prompt evaluation set to check hallucination + accuracy metrics for int8 vs int4.
- Fault tolerance: simulate GPU OOM and plan fallback (e.g., route to second node or degraded response with shorter token max).

Proposed pilot architecture (sketch):
- Appliance service (non-k8s): supervisor container that runs a model worker per GPU; mgmt API on internal port; local redis for in-proc prefix cache; startup script enforces CPU/GPU affinity.
- Model artifacts staged on local NFS share (no external internet). Signed manifests verified by HSM.
- Routing: lightweight NGINX + internal API; can expose token-limited SDK keys via their vault.
- Observability: local metric push to their Prometheus + node-exporter; we push a small agent to collect token latencies to our diagnostic dump (offline tar only).

Open questions for follow-up:
1) Confirm exact GPU model they plan to provision (A10, A5000, A100?) — affects memory budget and kernel support.
2) Do they want container-only install or will they accept a minimal k3s? (ops leaning: container-only).
3) HSM integration: vendor + API docs — need to verify signing flow with our artifact verification.
4) What are their retention and redaction rules for operator transcripts? Default retention 30d, but they asked 90d.
5) Are there hard SLAs for availability during shift hours? They implied yes for critical lines.

Immediate next steps (owners & dates):
- Prepare quick perf matrix (Lena) — run local bench: 7B-int8, 7B-int4, 13B-int8 on test node to estimate memory and latency by 2026-03-16.
- Draft appliance deployment doc (Marcus) — include NUMA tuning, container flags, supervisor config by 2026-03-20.
- Collect Oak Harbor HSM and staging-server spec (Priya) — ask for vendor docs + sample keys by 2026-03-12 (blocking).
- Create evaluation prompt set ingestion flow and test harness (Evan) — wire to our eval repo, provide result template by 2026-03-22.
- Legal: provide model license summary doc (Lena) — pull top 3 candidate model licenses and callouts by 2026-03-18.

Quick notes-to-self (informal):
- When measuring int4, capture token-level perplexity + repetition heuristics — we need something beyond simple BLEU.
- Watch for GPU clock-throttling in their environment; might need to recommend power profile.
- Consider offering a tiny hosted fallback (reduces their absolute isolation) — they'd likely reject but worth asking if they want redundancy.
- If NUMA issues persist, test with MIG (if GPUs support it) vs single-process memory mapping.

Meeting cadence proposal:
- Weekly 30-min sync with ops + ML (Mon 9am PT) for first 6 weeks.
- Biweekly deep-dive with infra + legal for rollout checklist.

Slack/threads to link in follow-up: #solutions-oak-harbor, #infra-embed (ask Marcus to drop perf traces), legal thread with model licenses.

End of scratchpad — keep this lean, move items to Confluence and Jira when stable.
